text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.38% today, continuing a strong two-week rally that's lifted the stock 10%. The sharp jump came on October 23rd when Brent crude oil spiked to a six-month high above $116 on escalating Middle East tensions—specifically rhetoric from the Trump administration about Iran market manipulation and concerns over Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. With crude still holding near $108 domestically and $115 globally, oil producers like ConocoPhillips benefit directly from higher prices, which expand their profit margins on every barrel extracted and sold.

The stock's momentum has proven resilient even as diplomatic efforts this week eased some of those tensions; a Saudi-Iran de-escalation meeting knocked oil lower on October 26–27, yet ConocoPhillips held its October 23rd gains. This suggests the market is pricing in persistent supply-chain risk in the region rather than treating the diplomatic news as a full reversal of the tension premium that sent oil higher in the first place.
